phase: Household Consumption — Borrower-Population Bridge Source Screening
purpose: Screen official household-level and household-budget sources for an observed Romania bridge between BNR housing-loan borrower DSTI and the registered aggregate S1M household-consumption target. This is source screening only; it does not construct weights, infer borrower consumption, or open estimation.

target_bridge.source_population: BNR respondent-bank housing/mortgage-loan borrowers represented by new/outstanding housing-loan DSTI
target_bridge.target_population: ESA S1M households + NPISH aggregate consumption
target_bridge.required_observation: An independently observed mapping, common microdata frame, or aligned borrower-subpopulation consumption/income target that links the housing-borrower burden population to the registered consumption population.

screened_sources.institution: European Central Bank / Household Finance and Consumption Network
participation_evidence: The ECB 2021-wave methodological report lists Banca Națională a României among HFCN member institutions, so network membership must not be confused with a Romania country dataset.
The ECB 2017-wave methodology states that the third wave covered all 19 euro-area countries plus Croatia, Hungary and Poland; Romania was not a participating survey country.
The ECB 2021-wave methodology states that the fourth wave covered all 19 euro-area countries plus Croatia, Czech Republic and Hungary; Romania was not a participating survey country.

The ECB 2023-wave results/methodology published in June 2026 state that the fifth wave covered the 20 euro-area countries at the time of collection plus Czech Republic and Hungary; Romania was not a participating survey country.
screened_sources.reason: HFCS is conceptually suitable and BNR participates in the HFCN network, but no Romania HFCS country dataset is identified in the 2017, 2021 or latest 2023 waves. Network membership therefore does not supply the required Romania microdata bridge.

Public TEMPO ABF tables identified in this screening provide quarterly consumption/budget measures and demographic/social breakdowns, but no observed grouping by mortgage-borrower status or linkage to the BNR DSTI population was identified.

Published CES income/spending series cover participating euro-area countries; no Romania country series was identified, and the survey would not by itself map BNR mortgage-borrower DSTI to aggregate S1M consumption.

screening_result.conclusion: No official public source identified in this screening closes the population boundary between BNR housing-loan DSTI and aggregate S1M consumption for Romania. HFCS remains conceptually suitable but has no Romania country dataset in the 2017, 2021 or latest 2023 wave; INS ABF public tables identified here do not stratify by mortgage-borrower status.

admissible_future_paths.trigger: Official/research microdata documentation demonstrates mortgage-borrower status together with compatible consumption/income variables and accessible survey weights.
BNR or another official source publishes a borrower-level or borrower-group consumption/income measure aligned to housing-loan DSTI.
An observed Romania household-sector debt-service burden aligned to S1M becomes available.

insufficient_evidence: Quarterly aggregate consumption from ABF or QSA without borrower-status stratification.
HFCS variable definitions from countries other than Romania.
Mortgage debt shares, homeownership rates or loan-stock shares used as synthetic population weights.
Correlation between housing-loan DSTI and aggregate consumption.
A longer DSTI time series without a population bridge.
